extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors of studies developing or validating multivariable prediction models (diagnostic or prognostic) in medicine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reporting studies that develop, validate, or update multivariable prediction models for diagnosis or prognosis in medical research, intended to ensure transparent and reproducible reporting. Applicable to both development and validation studies across all medical domains and predictor types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist of 22 items (TRIPOD Statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist of 22 items deemed essential for transparent reporting of a prediction model study; items relate to title/abstract, background/objectives, methods, results, discussion, and other information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the TRIPOD checklist (22 items) when reporting studies developing, validating, or updating multivariable prediction models; some items apply only to development studies (denoted D), some only to validation studies (V), and others to both (D;V). The checklist is a minimum set of information to be reported and is best used alongside the TRIPOD explanation and elaboration document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (items 1 and 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include essential information in the title and abstract to clearly identify the study as a development, validation, or update of a prediction model and to summarize objectives, participants, outcome, predictors, sample size, and main results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure the title and abstract enable readers and editors to quickly identify the study type and key elements; these are items 1 and 2 of the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and objectives (item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the scientific background, rationale, and specific objectives of the study, including whether the model is diagnostic or prognostic and whether the study concerns development, validation, or updating of a model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the intended use and target population of the model and position the work relative to existing models or predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe data sources and study participants (methods items 4–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report study design and source(s) of data, setting, eligibility criteria, recruitment/selection procedures, and relevant dates (e.g., periods of participant inclusion and follow-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe whether data are from cohorts, trials, registries, routine care, single or multicenter, and provide enough detail for replication and assessment of generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define outcome to be predicted
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly define the outcome (diagnostic or prognostic) including how and when it was measured and any reference standards used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For diagnostic studies the time window between predictor measurement and reference standard should be as short as possible and treatment should not start within this period; ensure clarity so others can replicate outcome assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly list candidate predictors and their measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report which predictors were considered, how and when they were measured, and any coding or transformations used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide definitions, measurement units, and handling of continuous predictors (e.g., categorization, transformations) so that others can reproduce predictor values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and events (sample size justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on sample size, number of outcome events, and rationale for the size relative to the number of candidate predictors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid small data sets with too few outcome events relative to the number of candidate predictors, which commonly leads to overfitting and optimistic performance estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and reporting of missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the amount of missing data for predictors and outcomes and describe methods used to handle missingness (e.g., complete-case, multiple imputation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor or inappropriate handling of missing data is a frequent deficiency; authors should report the method used and justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-building strategy and predictor selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the statistical model-building approach, including methods for selecting predictors (e.g., prespecification, stepwise selection), handling of interactions, and any rules used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the model-building strategy transparently; data-driven selection methods and lack of prespecification are common weaknesses and should be justified and described in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical model specification and choice (e.g., logistic, Cox)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the type of statistical model used (for example logistic regression for short-term outcomes, Cox regression for time-to-event outcomes) and all modeling choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail on model form so others can reproduce analyses (link functions, time scales, baseline hazard handling, software and packages used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal validation to quantify optimism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internal validation techniques (e.g., bootstrapping or cross-validation) within the original sample to quantify optimism in predictive performance and to assess overfitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal validation is a necessary part of model development; report the method used and the optimism-corrected performance estimates (for example bootstrap-corrected calibration and discrimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address overfitting and apply shrinkage/penalization as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and report approaches to reduce overfitting and optimism, such as shrinkage (heuristic or bootstrap-based) or penalization methods (ridge regression, lasso).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any shrinkage or penalization applied and rationale; these approaches can improve model calibration and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: External validation using original model formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate model performance in data other than that used for development by applying the original published regression formula to new individuals and comparing predicted with observed outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External validation can be temporal, geographic, setting-based, or population-based (e.g., adults → children) and is strongly recommended; report predictor and outcome definitions used in the validation data and any differences from development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model updating after validation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the model performs poorly on external validation, consider and report model updating or adjustment based on the validation dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the updating methods used (for example recalibration of intercept/slope, model revision) and present updated performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report participant flow and descriptive results (results items 13–17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numbers of participants at each stage, reasons for exclusions, baseline characteristics, and distributions of predictors and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent participant flow and descriptive statistics allow assessment of representativeness and applicability; include counts used in analyses and numbers with missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full model specification (coefficients and intercept/baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the full prediction model (regression coefficients, intercept or baseline survival) so that individual predictions can be calculated in other data or practice settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the full model (and/or web calculators, code) is important for reproducibility and for others to externally validate or implement the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report model performance measures (calibration, discrimination, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report measures of model predictive performance such as calibration and discrimination, with confidence intervals; distinguish apparent performance from optimism-corrected estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common performance metrics include calibration plots, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, c-statistic (AUC), and other appropriate measures for the outcome type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of limitations, interpretation, and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss strengths and limitations of the study, potential sources of bias, clinical implications, and generalizability of the model for intended use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place results in context of other models and evidence, and be explicit about appropriate use-case(s) and any caveats for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information: protocol, registration, funding, and supplementary materials (items 21–22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on study protocol availability, registration (if applicable), funding sources, and availability of supplementary materials (statistical code, full checklists, calculators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to develop and publish study protocols and to register observational prediction studies where possible; report funding sources and include a completed TRIPOD checklist as an additional file indicating pages where each item is reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of TRIPOD
rubrics_metrics.description: TRIPOD explicitly covers development and validation (and updating) of prediction models for diagnosis and prognosis across all medical domains and predictor types; it is not intended for etiologic studies or impact studies of using a model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use TRIPOD for reporting multivariable modeling aimed at causal/etiologic inference or for impact studies that quantify the effect of using a prediction model on outcomes; consider related guidelines (STROBE, REMARK, STARD, GRIPS) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the TRIPOD explanation and elaboration document
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the accompanying explanation and elaboration (E&E) document which explains each checklist item and provides examples of good reporting and descriptions of good practice versus limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The E&E contains examples from published articles and summarizes qualities of good (and limitations of less good) studies; it should be used alongside the checklist to guide reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD is a reporting guideline not a quality assessment tool
rubrics_metrics.description: TRIPOD provides guidance only for reporting research and does not prescribe how to develop or validate models nor should it be used to explicitly assess study quality or quantify risk of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an implicit expectation that appropriate study design and analyses have been conducted; for critical appraisal or systematic review data extraction use tools such as CHARMS or other risk-of-bias instruments as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to submit a completed checklist with manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid editorial review and readers, authors should submit the completed TRIPOD checklist as an additional file with the manuscript, indicating where information for each item is reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A TRIPOD reporting template is available for download from www.tripod-statement.org; journals are encouraged to request the checklist on submission.
